stories.standfirst: {winner} took season {seasonNo} of {seasonsTotal} by a margin that left {loser} studying the horizon from a very long way back.
paragraphs: Some seasons are contested and some are simply taken, and the one just ended belonged to the second kind. {winner}, guiding {winnerClub}, finished {margin} ahead of {loser}, a gap that needs no interpretation from this correspondent.

For {loserClub} the season offers little comfort, though rivalry is built on such reverses. A lead of this size shifts the whole weather of the contest, and {winnerPoints} against {loserPoints} reads as a record of authority rather than accident.
The reply now belongs to {loser}. Great rivalries are seldom settled by a single chapter, and {winnerClub} will know the next one is already being written.

pullquote.text: That was not a gap, it was a different postcode altogether.

stories.standfirst: Seldom does a season announce its winner so plainly, and {winnerClub} wore the finish as though it had been fitted for them.
paragraphs: The best campaigns settle their business early and spend the remainder in confirmation. So it proved for {winner}, whose {winnerClub} ended season {seasonNo} {margin} ahead of {loser} and {loserClub}, composed throughout and never once hurried.

What lingers is the ease of it. A rivalry between two friends usually lives on small edges, yet here the edge became a ridge, and {loser} must now study {winnerPoints} against {loserPoints} closely before the next chapter.
There remains plenty of Showdown left for the response, and {loser} is not a manager to treat such a gap as a final judgement, only as a very pointed question.

pullquote.text: You could have drawn the finish with a ruler on the first morning.

stories.standfirst: Built patiently and finished with confidence, {winner}'s season for {winnerClub} stands as the most commanding work in the Gazette's recent files.
paragraphs: Grand structures are rarely hurried, and {winner} has spent this season laying stone upon stone at {winnerClub}. The result, {margin} beyond the reach of {loser}, is less a finish than a finished building, handsome and load-bearing.

{loser} and {loserClub} will walk its corridors with mixed feelings, admiring the craft while measuring the walls. A margin of that height does not fall in one afternoon; it must be undermined slowly, season by season.
Season {seasonNo} of {seasonsTotal} has given this rivalry its first great edifice. Whether it becomes a monument or a ruin depends entirely on what {loser} builds in reply.

pullquote.text: A fine house, and the neighbours have noticed the extension.

stories.standfirst: Defeat is never gracious in its first hour, yet {loser} will find that a gap this wide can also be a map.
paragraphs: The headline belongs to {winner}, who carried {winnerClub} home {margin} in front of {loserClub} and {loser} at the close of season {seasonNo}. It was a performance of range and nerve, delivered without apparent strain.

Yet the story of any lopsided season is half told from the other side. {loser} has been shown, in plain figures, precisely what the standard is, and a manager who knows the standard can begin to plan for it.
Rivals rarely forget a season like this one, and the best of them use it. Expect {loserClub} to return with something sharper than sympathy.

pullquote.text: Nothing sharpens a pencil like a long way to travel.

stories.standfirst: One chapter of {seasonsTotal} has been written in {winner}'s hand, and the margin suggests the author had the ending half planned.
paragraphs: It is only season {seasonNo}, and the sensible reader will resist the word decisive. Still, {winner} and {winnerClub} have opened the account with {margin} to spare over {loser}, and a lead of that weight deserves to be taken seriously.

The shape of the Showdown now tilts. {loserClub} must chase where it expected to trade blows, and chasing is a different art, requiring patience as well as appetite. {winnerPoints} against {loserPoints} sets the terms.
Much remains on the calendar of this rivalry, and a lead this large can look either comfortable or heavy, depending on who is carrying it.

pullquote.text: A big lead is a loan, and somebody always comes to collect.
pullquote.who: The tea lady at the training ground

stories.standfirst: Balanced against everything {loser} could offer, the ledger for this season closes heavily in favour of {winnerClub}.
paragraphs: Audit the season line by line and the conclusion arrives quickly. {winner} brought {winnerPoints} to the account where {loser} brought {loserPoints}, and the resulting {margin} is the sort of surplus that needs no creative accounting.

For {loserClub} the entries are not shameful, merely outweighed. A rivalry like this keeps long books, and one lopsided page, however bold its figures, does not close a volume that still has many pages unturned.
The next audit falls due soon enough. {loser} will be hoping to present a more flattering set of accounts, and {winnerClub} will be hoping to avoid presenting any apology.

pullquote.text: Check the sums twice and they come out the same, sadly for one of us.

stories.standfirst: Two ships left harbour together in season {seasonNo}, but only {winnerClub} arrived with its colours flying and its hold full.
paragraphs: They sailed from the same port with the same hopes, and by the end of the voyage they were nowhere near each other. {winner} steered {winnerClub} home {margin} up on {loser}, a distance now visible only by telescope.

{loserClub} limped, perhaps, rather than sank, and there is dignity in that. The rivalry has not been lost; it has merely been given a headwind, and good captains regard headwinds as a chance to prove their seamanship.
Fresh charts will be drawn before the next departure. {loser} knows where the current runs strongest, and the Gazette expects a crowded and combative horizon.

pullquote.text: One of them is already talking about the next voyage, and it is not the winner.

stories.standfirst: The balance of power in this rivalry shifted a notch this season, and {winner} was the one holding the lever.
paragraphs: Balance, in a two-handed contest, is a delicate thing, and {winner} has leaned heavily on it. With {winnerClub} finishing {margin} above {loser}, the scales that hung level in conversation now lean decisively in one direction.
{loserClub} will know the sensation. To be outscored by such a gap invites reflection, and reflection, in a sporting rivalry, is often where the best resolve begins.
The scales may swing again, and swing violently. Season {seasonNo} of {seasonsTotal} has simply placed a heavy weight on one side, and the next season will test its fastenings.

pullquote.text: Scales love to tilt and hate to stay tilted for long.

stories.byline: Our man at the long game
stories.standfirst: A season like this tests a rival's character more than any close finish, and {loser} has the character to answer it.
paragraphs: {winner} deserves every line of praise. Season {seasonNo} was a clean, assured piece of work from {winnerClub}, and the {margin} that separates the pair is the evidence in full, easy to read and hard to dispute.

The question for {loser} is how quickly the disappointment becomes fuel. {loserClub} has shown resilience before, and a rivalry measured over {seasonsTotal} seasons rewards those who treat one bad page as a lesson rather than a sentence.
Pride is a patient motor. Expect {loser} to run it hard, and expect {winnerClub} to keep one eye on the mirror.

pullquote.text: The ones who lose big are the ones who learn big.
pullquote.who: The tea lady at the training ground

stories.standfirst: Order has been restored to the Showdown, though it is {winnerClub}'s order, and {loserClub} may feel it was imposed rather than agreed.
paragraphs: Few could argue with the arrangement of things at the close of season {seasonNo}. {winner} ranks first, {loser} ranks second, and between them sits a margin of {margin}, a gap with all the proportion of a well-built staircase.

It was not an accident of timing. {winnerClub} sustained its pace through the whole season while {loserClub} found the going heavier, and the final reckoning of {winnerPoints} against {loserPoints} records that difference faithfully.
Such order seldom lasts without challenge. The Gazette will be watching {loser} closely for the first sign of a rearrangement.

pullquote.text: Tidy, tidy work, and somebody is going to want to mess it up.

stories.standfirst: From the summit of season {seasonNo}, {winner} can see the whole range, and {loser} is still working out where the path begins.
paragraphs: Mountaineers speak of seasons in which every foothold holds, and this was one of them for {winner}. {winnerClub} reached the top {margin} ahead of {loser}, and had time enough to admire the view before the others arrived.

{loserClub} climbs on, naturally, and there is nothing unusual in being a camp or two behind. What matters is the route chosen next, because the same slope that favoured the leader can be turned to the pursuer's advantage.
Altitude brings its own dangers. {winner} will want to remember that the thinnest air is found at the top, and that {loser} is climbing.

pullquote.text: It is lovely up there until someone starts coming up behind you.

stories.standfirst: Respect, not ridicule, is due to {loser}, who pushed hard all season against a rival who simply had more to give.
paragraphs: Let it be said at the outset that {loserClub} did not fold. The season was full of honest effort from {loser}, but {winner} and {winnerClub} had more in reserve, finishing {margin} ahead in an outing of a very high order.

That is the honest story of a lopsided season: a good competitor meeting a better one on the day it mattered. {winnerPoints} against {loserPoints} flatters nobody and insults nobody; it is merely accurate.
Both managers will carry this one forward, one with confidence and one with purpose. The Gazette suspects the second may prove the more dangerous baggage.

pullquote.text: A good loser is only a winner who has not finished yet.

stories.byline: Special report from the map room
stories.standfirst: The cartographers of this rivalry will redraw their charts after season {seasonNo}, and {winnerClub} now occupies most of the paper.
paragraphs: Maps are only useful until the country changes. The country changed this season, when {winner} led {winnerClub} to a finish {margin} beyond {loser}, pushing the border of the possible far into rival territory.

{loserClub} remains a proud and well-defended neighbour, and nobody sensible would call its land conquered. But the frontier has moved, and a frontier that moves once can be persuaded to move back with enough resolve.
Expect fresh surveys before the next season. Both managers will be out measuring the ground, and only one of them will be doing it with a point to prove.

pullquote.text: Throw the old map away; the coastline has moved.

stories.standfirst: When the seasons of this Showdown are one day recounted, season {seasonNo} will be remembered as the one {winner} refused to share.
paragraphs: There is a certain kind of year that historians single out without being asked. {winner} made this one, taking {winnerClub} to a finish {margin} in front of {loser} and leaving little for the footnotes to argue about.

Yet {loserClub} should not be written off in the same stroke of the pen. History is generous to those who respond, and the very scale of this reverse may yet become the setting for a remarkable reply.
The record will show {winnerPoints} to {loserPoints}. What the record cannot show, not yet, is what {loser} intends to do about it.

pullquote.text: Mark this one in the margin, because there will be a reply.
pullquote.who: The tea lady at the training ground

stories.standfirst: A margin such as this is, among friends, less a debt than an invitation, and {loser} has been sent a handsome one.
paragraphs: Nobody in this contest takes a win like {winner}'s personally, or at least nobody admits to it. {winnerClub} finished {margin} up on {loserClub}, and the gracious reading is that it simply raised the bar for everyone.

A rivalry between friends thrives on exactly this: a gap to close, a reason to improve, and a fixed number of seasons in which to do something about it. {loser} will have all three on the desk this week.
So the invitation stands, printed in {winnerPoints} against {loserPoints}. Declining it would be most unlike this pair.

pullquote.text: Friends who win like that deserve to be chased, politely and with great speed.
